$comment: EL-5701 passenger elevator twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor come from the design data (load, counterweight balance, friction, door and energy baselines); the controller sends only what it measures.

identification.description: Passenger elevator 1 of the office tower lobby group: 12 stops, 44 m travel, machine-room-less traction
identification.machine: KONE EcoDisc gearless permanent-magnet hoisting machine in the shaft, double brake, steel ropes
identification.drive: VVVF (variable-voltage variable-frequency) regenerative drive, torque estimate per trip
identification.doors: Centre-opening car and landing doors, 900 mm clear opening, door operator with its own controller, curtain of light
identification.monitoring: Elevator controller and drive event log, car load weighing, car-top accelerometer (ride quality), energy meter on the lift supply

car.source: KONE MonoSpace 500 planning guide (kone.co.il, 2018) and UK brochure (kone.co.uk): rated load 1000 kg = 13 persons, car 1100 x 2100 mm, 1.6 m/s within the duty range (1000 kg, 75 m, 24 stops).

shaft.source: 12 stops at 4.0 m floor height (assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data); pit 1200 mm at 1.6 m/s from the KONE MonoSpace 500 planning guide (kone.co.il, 2018) and UK brochure (kone.co.uk).

hoist.source: Counterweight = car + 45 % of the rated load (balance ratio), traction sheave diameter, 2:1 roping and the running friction of guide shoes, rope bending and sheave bearings referred to the car (kN): assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data.

doors.source: Clear opening and type from the options of the KONE MonoSpace 500 planning guide (kone.co.il, 2018) and UK brochure (kone.co.uk). Opening time, closing time and the peak operator current on closing, measured at commissioning: assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data.

ride.source: Stopping accuracy +/-10 mm and levelling accuracy +/-20 mm: EN 81-70:2003 clause 5.3.3 (moved into EN 81-20 in 2018). Jerk and acceleration of the drive's travel curve: assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data.

brake.source: The daily automatic brake test of the drive (KONE EN 81-20 fact sheet: automated daily testing of brake torque). Reference torque = torque to hold 125 % of the rated load against the counterweight: assumption, a load ratio commonly used for brake checks; replace with your maker's test setting.

energy.source: Running energy per start (acceleration, braking, door cycle) and per metre travelled, and the standby power, measured on a reference cycle at commissioning in the way ISO 25745-1 describes: assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data. Annual energy by the ISO 25745-2 method is in the maker's EPD.

ropes.source: Expected rope life in trips for this sheave and roping: assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data (replace with the rope maker's or the lift maker's figure).

traffic.source: Rated starts per hour of the machine and drive: assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data.

demo.note: Demo only: the car serves a new call every few seconds whatever the hour so the 3D view is always moving; the counters (trips per day, starts per hour) follow an office day profile on the plant clock, with at least 60 starts per hour so the per-hour rates work at night.

limits.source: Alert limits: assumption: typical value, replace with your lift's commissioning report / maker's data. The stopping accuracy limit is EN 81-70:2003 5.3.3 (+/-10 mm, now in EN 81-20); ISO 18738-1 defines how ride vibration is measured but sets no limit, so the vibration limit is the commissioning baseline plus margin.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

door_obstruction.name: Door sill debris or worn door rollers
door_obstruction.symptoms: doors close slower and the operator draws more current to push them

light_curtain_fault.name: Light curtain dirty or misaligned
light_curtain_fault.symptoms: doors reopen on many closings with nobody in the way

door_lock_fault.name: Landing door lock contact fault
door_lock_fault.symptoms: door closes but the safety circuit stays open: retries, then the car is taken out of service

counterweight_imbalance.name: Counterweight out of balance (car mass changed)
counterweight_imbalance.symptoms: torque high on every up trip and low on every down trip by the same amount

guide_friction_high.name: Guide shoe wear or rail misalignment
guide_friction_high.symptoms: running friction up, torque up going up and down going down, car shakes sideways

brake_wear.name: Brake lining wear or brake spring weak
brake_wear.symptoms: the automatic brake test holds less torque each day

levelling_drift.name: Levelling drift (rope slip in worn sheave grooves, encoder)
levelling_drift.symptoms: the car stops further from the landing and re-levels more often

regen_lost.name: Regenerative drive not feeding back (energy burned in the resistor)
regen_lost.symptoms: energy per trip up at the same traffic
